to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business) and
Item Number you are commenting on. The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the
three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 1, 2021
   C. ADOPTION  OF RESOLUTION  NO.  21-26  APPROVING AN
  APPROPRIATION OF $65,000 TO FUND A FIBER OPTIC
  COMMUNICATIONS CONDUIT PROJECT ON LAS TUNAS DRIVE

  The Public Works Department is responsible for the maintenance of all the
  City’s streets and associated infrastructure including traffic signals. This work
  will extend the fiber optic network of the Measure R-funded fiber connectivity
  project already approved along Valley Boulevard and San Gabriel Boulevard,
  to include Las Tunas Drive from San Gabriel Boulevard to the western city
  limit.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-26 approving the re-appropriation of $65,000
  from the Del Mar bridge and Street Widening Capital Improvement
  Project account #122-800-50-97-650 for the purchase of the PVC pipe and
  accessories; and

  2. Approve the purchase of PVC pipe and accessories from Cal-Duct
  Incorporated in the amount of $60,402.96.

  D. ACCEPTANCE OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 74474 (1315 PALM AVENUE)
  PLANNING CASE NO. PL-16-111

  The development, located at 1315 Palm Avenue, is a four-unit condominium
  development on a 17,529 square foot lot. Staff and the City’s contract
  consultant for land surveying, RKA Consulting Group, Incorporated, have
  reviewed the Final Parcel Map and have determined it is in compliance with
  the State Subdivision Map Act, conditions of approval, and the City’s
  Ordinances regarding subdivision.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept the Final Parcel Map No. 74474
  and authorize filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder.

  3
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 1, 2021
   E. ACCEPTANCE OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 76058 (415 WEST RALPH
  STREET) PLANNING CASE NO. PL-17-067

  The development, located at 415 West Ralph Street, is a two-unit
  condominium development on a 9,804 square foot lot. Staff and the City’s
  contract consultant for land surveying, RKA Consulting Group, Incorporated,
  have reviewed the Final Parcel Map and have determined it is in compliance
  with the State Subdivision Map Act, conditions of approval, and the City’s
  Ordinances regarding subdivision.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept the Final Parcel Map No. 76058
  and authorize filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder.

  F. CONTRACT EXTENSION OF PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES WITH
  INTER-CON SECURITY SYSTEMS INCORPORATED IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $275,864 ANNUALLY

  The City of San Gabriel is a densely-populated and heavily-visited community.
  There is multiple areas with various zoning components that are experiencing
  increased traffic congestion and parking complaints. Additionally, the City
  hosts a large number of visitors who patronize various commercial areas,
  creating the need for focused parking enforcement activities to maintain
  traffic flow, traffic safety, and parking rotations, while balancing the quality of
  life for residents. The agreement provides private parking enforcement
  officer(s) during stipulated hours for parking enforcement activities and they
  issue an average of approximately 1300 citations per month for various
  parking violations.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to
  exercise the option of extending the current contract for two additional years
  with Inter-Con Security Systems Incorporated for parking enforcement
  services and execute the contract amendment on behalf of the City.

  4
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 1, 2021
   G. ACCEPTANCE OF ASSISTANCE TO FIREFIGHTERS GRANT – 2020 COVID-
  19 SUPPLEMENTAL

  The City of San Gabriel has been awarded $11,047.05 for the San Gabriel Fire
  Department from the Assistance to Firefighters Supplemental (AFG-S) 2020
  COVID-19 Grant Program administered by the Federal Emergency
  Management Agency (FEMA). The City of San Gabriel is required to provide a
  10% match and will purchase half-mask respiratory protective equipment
  with the funding from this grant.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-25
  approving the following:

  1. Increase account #186-3212 by $11,047.05 (revenue account);
  2. Increase the Fire Department budget by $11,047.05 in account #124-761-
  57-99-390; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee, the Fire Chief, to accept the
  Assistance to Firefighters Supplemental (AFG-S) grant and purchase the
  items under the City’s purchasing policy.

  H. APPROVE AGREEMENT WITH SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HUMANE SOCIETY
  (SGVHS) IN THE AMOUNT OF $255,000 FOR ANIMAL CARE AND
  CONTROL SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021-22

  At the direction of the City Council, staff has researched alternatives for
  provision of animal care and control services to manage increased service
  costs. The San Gabriel Valley Humane Society (SGVHS) has provided Animal
  Care and Control services to the City for many decades. Staff has researched
  alternatives and has determined that the SGVHS proposal is the most viable
  and cost-effective option. Staff seeks Council’s approval on an agreement
  with SGVHS for Animal Care and Control Services for the 2021-22 fiscal year
  with an option to extend for one year.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a contract with San Gabriel Valley Humane Society for a full-service model for
  the 2021-2022 Fiscal Year with an option to extend for one additional year.

  5
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 1, 2021
   I. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH WILLIAM HEZMALHALCH
  ARCHITECTS FOR ARCHITECTURAL, URBAN DESIGN, AND HISTORIC
  PRESERVATION PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

  On January 4, 2021, the City of San Gabriel issued a Request for Proposals
  (RFP No. 21-01) for a qualified firm to provide architectural, urban design, and
  historic preservation professional services. The City received six proposals and
  William Hezmalhalch Architects best met the criteria outlined in the RFP. A
  not-to-exceed in the amount of $40,000 yearly for a three-year period,
  inclusive of all costs and services through June 1, 2024 has been
  recommended.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with William Hezmalhalch Architects and authorize the City
  Manager to execute said agreement and issue a purchase order in the amount
  of $40,000.

  J. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 21-24 TO ACCEPT DONATION IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $2,000 FROM ATHENS SERVICES AND INCREASE BUDGET
  BY $9,200 FOR KABOOM! PLAYGROUND BUILD AT ROOSEVELT PARK

  In November 2019, the Community Services Department submitted a
  KABOOM! Grant application for a new playground at Roosevelt Park. In
  September 2020, the City Council approved the Letter of Intent with
  KABOOM!, Incorporated so that the City’s project would be included on a list
  of “shovel-ready” projects. Later that month, KABOOM! confirmed that the
  City had an interested funding partner, Blue Shield of California. In December
  2020, installation of the new Roosevelt Park playground began.

  During the brief preparation time for the playground, staff worked to bring in
  a sponsor to help fund the project. Athens Services was supportive and
  contributed financially to this project. The cost to the City for the new
  playground is $9,200.00.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends approval of the following:

  1. Accept the donation totaling $2,000 and increase account #121-850-10-
  21-000 by that same amount; and

  6
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 1, 2021
   2. Adopt Resolution No. 21-24 to increase appropriations from the General
  Fund by $2,000 and Park Impact Fee Fund by $7,200 for a total budget
  increase of $9,200 for the playground equipment at Roosevelt Park.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION  OF  PROPOSED  OPERATING  BUDGET,  CAPITAL
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM, FEE SCHEDULE AND APPROPRIATIONS
  LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021-22 AND FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE
  NO. 672 INSTITUTING A CANDIDATE FILING FEE FOR CANDIDATES FOR
  ELECTIVE OFFICE AND ORDINANCE NO. 673 AMENDING CHAPTER 9 OF
  THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO ALARM PERMITS

  Select the links below to access the staff report and attachments.

  Staff Report  City Council  Fire
  Budget Message  Administration  Community Development
  Budget Summaries  City Clerk  Public Works

  The City Council will hold a Public Hearing to consider adoption of the
  Proposed Operating Budget, Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), Appropriations
  Limit and Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2021-22. The operating budget is
  balanced, with revenues totaling $81,196,446 and expenditures totaling
  $67,261,477. The General Fund is also balanced, with $48,191,860 in revenues
  and $43,876,659 in expenditures. The CIP totals $21,396,700, for 27 projects,
  utilizing a combination of new revenues and existing fund balances. The
  Appropriations Limit is calculated at $46,355,277. The Proposed Fee Schedule
  requires amendments to the San Gabriel Municipal Code, which are proposed
  in Ordinance Nos. 672 and 673, which will be introduced for first reading.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing on the
  Proposed 2021-22 Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budgets,
  Fee Schedule and related Ordinances, and Appropriations Limit, and after
  receiving comments and testimony adopt the following resolutions:

  7
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 1, 2021
   Resolution No. 21-22 adopting the City of San Gabriel Fiscal Year 2021-22
  Operating Budget

  Resolution No. 21-23 approving the City of San Gabriel 2020-21 to 2024-
  25 Five-Year Capital Improvement Program and adopting the 2021-22
  Capital Improvement Program Budget

  Resolution No. 21-20 establishing the City of San Gabriel’s appropriation
  limit for the Fiscal Year 2021-22

  Resolution No. 21-21 adopting the Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2021-22

  It is further recommended that the City Council introduce the following
  Ordinances for first reading by title only:

  Ordinance No. 672 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City
  of San Gabriel, California, Instituting a Candidate Filing Fee for Candidates
  for Elective Office”

  Ordinance No. 673 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City
  of San Gabriel, California, Amending Chapter 91 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code Relating to Alarm Permits”

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. 21-19 EXPRESSING A VOTE OF
  NO CONFIDENCE IN LOS ANGELES COUNTY DISTRICT ATTORNEY
  GEORGE GASCÓN FOR HIS ATTEMPT TO UNDERMINE LEGISLATION
  AND THE BALLOT INITIATIVE PROCESS AND PLACE THE SAFETY OF THE
  GENERAL PUBLIC AT RISK

  At the May 4, 2021 regular City Council meeting, the City Council requested
  an item to discuss a resolution adopting a Vote of No Confidence in Los
  Angeles County District Attorney George Gascón be placed on a future
  regular City Council meeting. The item was considered at the May 18, 2021
  City Council meeting but technological issues with the City’s streaming service
  required the meeting to be adjourned before discussion on the item was
  complete.

  Recommended Action:

  8
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 1, 2021
   Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the attached Resolution No.
  21-19 and consider adopting it. Alternatively, the City Council could choose
  to adopt the alternate resolution, modify the language in either resolution, or
  to take no action at all on the item.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 674
  AMENDING CHAPTER 92 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  INCLUDE VOLUNTARY CAT LICENSING

  At the April 20, 2021 City Council Regular Meeting, City Council directed staff
  to return with an ordinance for voluntary cat licensing as an additional service
  to residents to be administered through the San Gabriel Valley Humane
  Society (SGVHS). Currently, the City of San Gabriel does not provide a cat
  licensing service option. Adoption of this Ordinance would add voluntary cat
  licensing to help support animal care and control in the community and
  facilitate reuniting cats with their owners.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council introduce for first reading by title only
  Ordinance No. 674 amending Title IX Chapter 92 of the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code establishing voluntary cat licensing.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of

  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, June 15, 2021, at

MINUTES OF JUNE 1, 2021
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  Mayor Liao called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:33 P.M.
  on Tuesday, June 1, 2021 , with all Council Members and staff participating by
  teleconference.

  INITIATIVE PROCESS AND PLACE THE SAFETY OF THE GENERAL PUBLIC AT
  RISK

  Chief City Clerk Clark explained that at the May 18, 2021 City Council meeting,
  Council Member Harrington presented this item and Los Angeles County Deputy
  District Attorney Eric Siddall, as Vice President of the Association of Deputy District

I  Attorneys, provided his Association's perspective. However, the item was not
  concluded as technical difficulties interrupted the live-streaming of the meeting.

  Council Member Harrington and Mr. Siddall provided a brief presentation on the
  item.

  Clarification discussion included crime-related voter initiatives; prosecutorial,
  judicial, corrections, gubernatorial and law enforcement discretion and related
  consequences; factors related to juvenile offenders; the DA's declination to send a
  representative to this meeting; the effect of the DA's special directives on
  deterrence, rehabilitation, and justice reform; public defenders as the beneficiaries
  of the special directives; effects of Propositions 47 and 57 and Assembly Bill (AB)
  109 on crime overall; increase in declination to prosecute crimes committed in San
  Gabriel pursuant to the DA's special directives; diversion programs; the DA's
  mandates versus discretionary actions as related to the special directives;
  alternatives to and after incarceration; possible impact to the City in relation to
  taking a position opposing the DA's policies; San Gabriel Police Department's
  juvenile diversion activities; a request to agendize an update on crime in the City;
  a rise in crime rate associated with societal re-opening; and post-incarceration

I  supeNision and assistance.
